name: Admin operates the live operations dashboard
description: Verifies every primary administrator dashboard tile opens a usable operational surface instead of acting as decorative UI.
steps: Sign in with an approved Nightjar administrator email
Open Listener People, Creator People and Administrator People
Open Creator Approvals and inspect the queue
Open Revenue, Subscriptions and Listening Economics
expected: Each administrator tile opens a functional view or protected operational destination, and no tile relies on a notification-only placeholder.

name: Admin previews every account role without changing administrator access
description: Verifies the administrator can inspect all role-facing product surfaces while the real backend role remains Administrator.
steps: Open Admin as an approved administrator
Preview Writer and create a local draft in preview
Preview Editor and inspect the editorial queue
expected: Each role preview renders its own surface, the preview banner identifies the real Administrator role, and returning to Admin restores the operational dashboard.

name: Creator sees transparent listening economics and protected script access
description: Verifies the Creator surface presents listening and revenue attribution while keeping manuscript copy and export permissions separate.
expected: Creator Studio shows listening and attribution information, and the protected script remains readable with copy and export off.

name: Use the Protection Centre
description: Verifies a signed-in user can submit a protection report and inspect supporting evidence without exposing clipboard contents.
expected: Nightjar creates a case ID, the case appears in My Cases, and evidence records are available as supporting signals.

name: Normal account cannot access administrator overview
description: Verifies administrator-only operational data is not available to a normal listener or creator account.
steps: Sign in with a normal Nightjar account
Open the account as a Listener
expected: The normal account remains outside the administrator area and cannot access administrator-only People, approvals or subscription data.

name: Every account can build a personalised Nightjar profile
description: Verifies the shared identity layer is available independently of account role.
steps: Set a chosen name and unique @handle
Add favourite tags, tropes and categories
expected: The personalised profile persists and remains separate from the account's permission role.

name: Protected script activity creates an all-owner security alert
description: Verifies qualifying protected-content activity becomes a retained security alert addressed to all three Nightjar owners.
steps: Open a protected script with an approved account
Generate qualifying high-volume protected-content events in a test environment
expected: A retained security alert identifies the account/session/script signals and records both owner recipients; an administrator can suspend the account, which revokes active reader sessions.

name: People directory represents every Nightjar account role
description: Verifies administrator People is a real five-role directory rather than an administrator-only/partial list.
expected: All five roles have dedicated directory surfaces, counts come from real account data except the three configured owner administrators, and no fake account records are created.

name: Administrator allowlist includes all Nightjar owners
description: Verifies every configured Nightjar owner is represented as an administrator and that owner-only security controls use the same allowlist.
steps: Sign in with each approved Nightjar owner email in a test environment
expected: All three approved owner accounts are represented as active Administrators, and security alerts are addressed to the same three configured owners.

name: Age verification persists on the Nightjar account
description: Verifies a completed 18+ age check is stored against the Nightjar account and is reused on later authentication without creating a new verification session.
steps: Sign in to a fresh test account
Complete the Yoti sandbox age check
Confirm Nightjar marks the account VERIFIED
Sign in again with the same account
Open Nightjar on another browser/device using the same account
expected: The account remains age verified after sign-out, subsequent sign-in and device change; Nightjar does not open a new age-verification session unless reverifyRequired is explicitly set.

name: Unverified account cannot retrieve adult catalogue content
description: Verifies the backend does not rely solely on the client-side age gate and blocks adult catalogue retrieval for an authenticated but unverified account.
steps: Sign in with an authenticated test account that has not completed age verification
Call the adult catalogue endpoint again
expected: The first catalogue request returns an age-verification-required response and no adult release payload; after verified state is stored, the same account can retrieve the catalogue without another verification.

name: Inclusive spotlight system gives everyone a fair daily lane
description: Verifies the discovery page has separate Listener, Creator and Writer spotlight lanes. Creators and Writers rotate through every active public member one full day at a time; listeners use the previous completed week's top seven and rotate one per day.
steps: Open the Nightjar discovery page as an age-verified account
Inspect Creator Spotlight, Writer Spotlight and Listener Spotlight
Confirm the Creator slot changes to the next active Creator on the following day
Confirm the Writer slot changes to the next active Writer on the following day
Confirm Listener Spotlight identifies the weekly Top 7 cohort and one listener occupies each day of the seven-day cycle
Complete a new week and confirm the listener cohort is refreshed from the newly completed week's listening activity
expected: All three lanes are visible when eligible members/data exist. Creator and Writer rotations are deterministic and give each eligible public member a complete day; the Listener seven remains fixed for the week and refreshes as a new cohort on the following week.

name: Listener spotlight ranking uses tracked listening from the previous completed week
description: Verifies Listener Spotlight is based on listener-role tracked activity from the previous completed Monday-Sunday period rather than changing mid-week.
steps: Seed a test week with tracked listening events for more than seven active Listener accounts
Inspect the selected listener and Top 7 metadata
Repeat the request during the same week after additional listening activity is recorded
Advance to the following Monday and request Spotlight again
expected: The same seven listeners remain the eligible cohort throughout the week and are shown one per day. The following Monday uses the newly completed week's ranking instead. Accounts with public profiles disabled are not exposed as spotlight profiles.

name: Spotlighted users receive one idempotent daily notification
description: Verifies the daily spotlight service creates an in-app notification for each spotlighted account, with creator/writer promotion messaging and a listener thank-you message, without duplicating the same notification on repeated reads.
steps: Use a test environment with an eligible Creator, Writer and Listener Spotlight
Open the discovery page twice on the same day
Sign in as each spotlighted account and open Notifications
Inspect the Creator and Writer notifications
Repeat the spotlight request several times
expected: Each spotlighted account has one notification for that day's spotlight. Creator and Writer messages invite natural discovery/share of their work; Listener messaging thanks them for contributing to the community. Repeated spotlight reads do not create duplicate notifications.

name: Creator and Writer spotlights provide natural sharing promotion
description: Verifies today's Creator and Writer spotlight cards expose a share action using the device/browser share mechanism where supported and a clipboard fallback otherwise.
steps: Open a discovery page containing the Creator Spotlight
Use Share spotlight and confirm the message identifies today's Creator Spotlight and Nightjar
Use Share spotlight and confirm the message identifies today's Writer Spotlight and Nightjar
expected: Creator and Writer spotlight cards provide an optional, user-triggered share action. The generated message promotes the featured person and Nightjar without forcing a share or fabricating engagement.

name: Creator and Writer rotation reaches every roster member
description: Guards against a weekday-only rotation that would stop at the first seven people. The rotation must use the absolute calendar day against the full eligible roster.
steps: Seed more than seven active public Creator accounts and more than seven active public Writer accounts
Inspect the daily spotlight for successive calendar days
Continue until every eligible member has received a spotlight day
expected: The rotation advances across the entire eligible Creator roster and entire eligible Writer roster, including members beyond the first seven. No member is skipped solely because the roster exceeds seven.

name: Small spotlight rosters cycle continuously without empty days
description: Verifies that a roster smaller than seven still produces a spotlight every calendar day. Once every eligible person has had a day, the same roster begins again immediately.
steps: Seed three active public Creator accounts and three active public Writer accounts
Inspect the spotlight on six consecutive calendar days
Inspect the spotlight on the seventh and eighth days
expected: The first three days feature Creator 1, Creator 2 and Creator 3, then the sequence repeats from Creator 1 on day four. Writer rotation behaves independently in the same continuous manner. There are no empty days caused by the roster being smaller than seven.

name: Listener Top 7 repeats when fewer than seven eligible listeners exist
description: Verifies that a weekly listener cohort smaller than seven still uses every available listener without creating placeholder days.
steps: Seed three eligible Listener accounts with tracked activity in the completed week
Open Listener Spotlight across the seven days of the current week
expected: The three listeners are rotated across the available days using the same cohort repeatedly; no empty placeholder listener is introduced simply because the cohort contains fewer than seven people.

name: Background scheduler materializes spotlight notifications without a page load
description: Verifies the daily scheduled job can create the same day’s spotlight notifications even when nobody has opened the discovery page first.
steps: Run the scheduled spotlight job for a test day with eligible Creator, Writer and Listener targets
Do not open the discovery page before the job runs
Sign in as each spotlight target and open Notifications
expected: Each spotlight target already has the correct daily notification before any discovery-page request occurs.

name: Scheduled spotlight materialization is protected by GitHub OIDC
description: Verifies the background endpoint only accepts a short-lived GitHub Actions OIDC token issued for the Nightjar main branch workflow.
steps: Call the internal spotlight scheduler endpoint without a token
Call it with an invalid token
Run the main-branch scheduled workflow with the GitHub id-token permission
expected: Unauthenticated and invalid requests are rejected; a valid token bound to the Nightjar repository, main branch and approved audience is accepted.

name: Repeated scheduled spotlight runs remain idempotent
description: Guards against duplicate notifications when the two midnight safety runs or a retried scheduled job hit the same London calendar day.
steps: Run the spotlight scheduler twice for the same London day
Open Notifications for each spotlight target
expected: Each target has exactly one notification for that spotlight date and kind; retries only report already-materialized work.

name: Creator audio upload detects duration and persists media assets
description: Verifies Creator Studio can turn a real media file into a stored release asset and record readable duration metadata.
steps: Confirm duration is detected when media metadata is readable
expected: The release retains stored audio/artwork URLs, readable audio duration is recorded, and the release remains private until submitted.

name: Creator submissions cannot bypass content moderation
description: Verifies complete creator releases enter the moderator queue instead of becoming public immediately.
steps: Complete title, description, category and audio
Choose Approve, Request changes or Reject
expected: Submission becomes pending_review; only an administrator decision can publish it, return it to draft with feedback, or reject it; the creator receives a notification.

name: Nightjar player resumes and queues real listening
description: Verifies the shared player behaves like a real listening surface and feeds the listening model.
steps: Navigate next and previous where multiple releases exist
expected: A valid incomplete listening position resumes, completed releases reopen from the beginning, progress/completion events are recorded, and queue navigation changes the active release.

name: Creator public profile contains only public released work
description: Verifies public Creator discovery is a real destination without leaking private drafts.
steps: Open a public Creator from the directory or spotlight
expected: Only public profile fields and released catalogue records are shown; drafts remain hidden, follow state persists, and sharing uses a supported destination.

name: Writer discovery separates public identity from protected writing
description: Verifies Writers can be promoted without exposing manuscript text or production permissions.
steps: Set a Writer profile to public
Open Writer discovery as a listener
expected: Public identity, profile copy and creative focus may appear; protected manuscript content and collaboration permissions do not.

name: Onboarding stores explicit preferences without inferring identity
description: Verifies the new modular question surface treats identity and taste as explicit user choices.
expected: Saved answers persist to the account, public visibility remains controlled by the user, and skipped onboarding is not falsely marked complete.

name: Completed listening does not resume at the end of the release
description: Guards against reopening a completed release at its terminal position.
expected: The resume endpoint returns zero position for the completed release so the next listen starts from the beginning.

name: Recommendation feedback tunes the taste graph
description: Verifies recommendation feedback is recorded as a durable preference signal and remains separate from identity fields.
steps: Choose Less like this on another release
Choose Not for me on a third release
expected: Feedback is persisted, Not for me suppresses the selected release, and later recommendations use the explicit signals without changing identity data.

name: Recommendation diversity prevents creator concentration
description: Verifies a highly productive creator cannot occupy the whole personalised shelf when other eligible releases exist.
steps: Seed several releases from one creator and releases from other creators
expected: The recommendation shelf limits repeated releases from one creator and continues filling from other eligible creators.

name: Listening telemetry does not treat progress ticks as taste
description: Verifies frequent playback progress events are stored for listening analytics but do not create repeated positive taste signals.
steps: Play one release for more than a minute
expected: Progress events exist for resume and listening analytics, while taste signals are generated only from meaningful listening actions such as start, completion, replay or skip.

name: Recommendation feedback is modular and immediately actionable
description: Verifies each personalised release exposes compact feedback controls without coupling feedback state to the main application shell.
steps: Use More, Less and Not for me controls
Confirm the selected release reacts without navigating away
expected: Feedback controls are available on the release card, provide a visible acknowledgement and Not for me removes that release from the current shelf.
